title: 47 Swahili Phrases in 11 Minutes | Learn Swahili for Beginners (Self Improvement)
description:
Learn 47 essential Swahili phrases in 11 minutes - the fun, fast way.
#Swahili #LearnSwahili #LanguageLearning

Every phrase follows the same rhythm: hear it in English, hear it in Kiswahili, then say it out loud with the pronunciation guide. Perfect for beginners, travellers and anyone who wants to speak Swahili with confidence.

WHAT YOU GET
- 8 themed chapters, 47 real-life phrases
- Kiswahili audio from a native voice
- English pronunciation guide for every line
- A brand-new lesson every single day

CHAPTERS
0:07  Self Improvement · Kujiboresha
1:33  Dating & Romance · Uchumba na Mapenzi
2:52  Balance · Usawa
4:12  Travel & Airport · Usafiri na Uwanja wa Ndege
5:31  Cultural Traditions · Jadi za Kitamaduni

8:09  Banking & Money · Benki na Pesa
9:27  Positive Life · Maisha Chanya

PHRASE LIST

SELF IMPROVEMENT · Kujiboresha
• Replace one excuse with action. - Badili visingizio kimoja, fanyia kazi sasa.  [badILI visINGIZIO kiMOJA, fANYiA KAZi sasa.]
• Make your bed, claim momentum. - Tengeneza kitanda chako, jizungumze kwa hatua.  [TENGeneza kiTANda chako, jizungUMbe kwa HATUA.]
• Turn off notifications for one hour. - Zima arifa kwa saa moja, utulize akili.  [ziMA aRIFA kwa saa MOJA, uTULize AKeLI.]
• Clean one task, then rest. - Maliza jambo moja, kisha pumzika bila hatia.  [maLIZA JAMbo MOJA, KISHA pUMzika biLA haTIA.]
• Plan your commute, save your mind. - Panga safari yako, ili ubaki mtulivu njiani.  [panGA SAfaRI yaKO, ILI uBaki mTULivu nJANI.]
• Practice gratitude before you sleep. - Shukuru kabla ya kulala, andika mawazo matatu.  [shUkuRU biLAA ya kuLAla, aNdiKA maWAZO maTATU.]

DATING & ROMANCE · Uchumba na Mapenzi
• Would you like to dance with me? - Je, ungetaka kucheza dansi pamoja nami?  [Je, ungetaka kucheza DANSI pamoja NAMi?]
• Are you free for a date soon? - Una muda bure kwa tarehe hivi karibuni?  [Una MUDA bure kwa TAREHE hivi karibuni?]
• Let’s meet at seven, just us. - Tuonane saa saba, sisi tu.  [Tuanane saa SABA, sisi TU.]
• I like your laugh, it’s contagious. - Napenda kicheko chako, kinatia moyo sana.  [N a Penda KICHEKO chako, kiNATIa MOYO saNA.]
• Tell me your favorite love song. - Niambie wimbo wako unaoupenda wa mapenzi.  [NiaMBIE wimbo wako unaoUPENDA wa maPENZI.]
• Can we watch the sunset together? - Tunaweza kutazama jua linapozama pamoja?  [Tu-naWEZA kutazama JUA linapoZAMA pamoja?]

BALANCE · Usawa
• Let your breath steady you first. - Chukua pumzi, ikutie utulivu kwanza.  [Chukua PUMZI, ikutie u-TULIVU KWAANZA.]
• I pause before I react. - Ninasitisha kabla sijajibu kwa hasira.  [Na-si-TISH-a KA-bla SI-ja-JIBU kwa HA-si-ra.]
• Balance your meal, not just quantity. - Usawa wa mlo wako ni zaidi ya kiasi tu.  [U-sawa wa MO-lo wa-ko ni ZAIDI ya KI-si-cha tu.]
• Switch off, then come back calm. - Zima simu, kisha urudi kwa utulivu.  [ZI-ma si-mu, KISHA u-RU-di kwa u-TU-LI-VU.]
• Slow hands, steady heart today. - Mikono polepole, moyo thabiti leo.  [Mi-KO-no PO-le-po, MO-yo THA-biti LEO.]
• I keep my promises, softly. - Nashikilia ahadi zangu, kwa upole.  [Na-shi-KI-li-a A-HI-di za-ngu, kwa u-PO-le.]

TRAVEL & AIRPORT · Usafiri na Uwanja wa Ndege
• Where is security screening for exits? - Usalama uko wapi kwa ajili ya kuingia?  [Usalama UKO wapi kwa ajili ya kuingia?]
• How early should I arrive? - Nifikie hapa mapema kiasi gani?  [Nifikie HAPA mapema kiasi gani?]
• Is my gate on the board? - Je, lango langu litaonekana kwenye ubao?  [Je, LANGO langu litaonekana kwenye UBAO?]
• What time does boarding start? - Kupanda ndege kunaanza saa ngapi?  [Ku-PANDA ndege kunaANZA saa ngapi?]
• Can I get assistance for my disability? - Naomba msaada kwa kiti changu cha ulemavu.  [Naomba MSAAda kwa kiti changu cha ULEMAVU.]
• Is there a pharmacy inside the airport? - Kuna duka la dawa hapa ndani ya uwanja wa ndege?  [Kuna DUKA la DAWA hapa ndani ya Uwanja wa NDEGE?]

CULTURAL TRADITIONS · Jadi za Kitamaduni
• We brew strong kahawa for visitors. - Tunapika kahawa nene kuwakaribisha wageni.  [Tunaa-Pi-ka KAH-a-wa NEN-e ku-wa-KA-ri-bi-sha WA-ge-ni.]
• We pour water first, then greet. - Tunamimina maji kwanza, kisha tunasalimia.  [Tu-na-mi-mi-na MA-ji KWAN-za, KI-sha TU-na-sa-limi-a.]
• At home we welcome with a smile. - Nyumbani tunawakaribisha kwa tabasamu.  [NYU-mba-ni tu-na-wa-ka-ribi-sha kwa ta-ba-SAA-mu.]
• We share dates during long visits. - Tunagawana tende wakati wa ziara ndefu.  [Tu-na-ga-wa-na TEN-de WI-ka-ti wa ZI-a-ra nDEF-u.]
• Before meals, we thank together quietly. - Kabla ya chakula, tunashukuru pamoja kwa utulivu.  [KAB-la ya CHA-ku-la, tu-na-SHU-ku-ri pamwe kwa u-tu-LI-vu.]
• We sing a short work song together. - Tunaimba wimbo mfupi wa kazi pamoja.  [Tu-na-IM-ba WI mbo m-FU-Pi wa KAA-zi pa-mO-a.]
